Extract matches of token patterns and phrases from texts using spaCy

Source: R/spacy_extract_matches.R
spacy_extract_matches.Rd

Find sequences of tokens that match patterns, using spaCy's rule-based Matcher (see https://spacy.io/usage/rule-based-matching). A pattern describes each token of a sequence by its attributes, which can be those that the language model assigns, such as the part of speech or the dependency relation. Phrases, and the values of a quanteda dictionary, can be matched too. Unlike the patterns given to spacy_initialize() as entity_patterns, these do not change the pipeline or the entities of a document.

Usage

spacy_extract_matches(
  x,
  patterns,
  overlap = c("all", "longest", "first"),
  n_process = 1L,
  batch_size = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a character object or a TIF-compliant corpus data.frame (see https://github.com/ropensci/tif)

patterns

the patterns to match, either:

  • a named list, in which each name is the label of a pattern, and each element is a token pattern in spaCy's structure: a list with one named list of attributes for each token, such as list(list(LOWER = "new"), list(LOWER = "york")). An element can also be a list of such token patterns, which are then alternatives for that label. The names must be unique.

  • a spacyr_entity_patterns object from as_entity_patterns(), whose labels become the labels of the matches. Patterns with the same label are alternatives for that label, and the IDs of the patterns are ignored. The object can hold phrases as well as token patterns; this is the way to match phrases, exactly or, with case_insensitive = TRUE, in any case.

  • a quanteda dictionary, which is converted with as_entity_patterns() and its defaults: the top-level keys are the labels, and values match in any case, with wildcards as in quanteda. Call as_entity_patterns() yourself to change these.

overlap

which matches to return where matches of the same label overlap: "all" (the default) returns every match, including those inside or overlapping another, as spaCy does; "longest" keeps the longest of them, and "first" the one that starts first. Matches of different labels can overlap whatever the value.

n_process

the number of processes for spaCy's nlp.pipe() to use: 1 (the default) processes the documents in the current R session's Python process, a larger number starts that many Python processes, and -1 uses all CPUs. Starting the processes and loading the model in each takes time, so more than one process helps only for large numbers of documents. A custom pipeline component must be defined in an importable Python module to be used in other processes.

batch_size

the number of documents that spaCy's nlp.pipe() processes together; NULL (the default) uses the pipeline's default (nlp.batch_size). Larger batches can be faster, but use more memory.

...

unused

Value

A data.frame with one row for each match, and no rows when nothing matches:

doc_id

the document

sentence_id, token_id

the sentence of the first token of the match, and the position of that token in its sentence, both starting at 1 as in spacy_parse(). A match that crosses a sentence boundary is given the sentence of its first token. Both are NA when the document has no sentence boundaries, as when the pipeline has neither a parser nor a sentence segmenter.

label

the label of the pattern that matched. It does not say which of a label's alternative patterns matched, which spaCy does not report.

text

the matched text

start_id

the position of the first token of the match in the document, starting at 1, as in spacy_extract_entity()

length

the number of tokens matched

Rows are in the order of the documents in x; within a document, by start_id, then by length (the shortest first), then by the order of the labels in patterns. The order does not depend on overlap.

Details

Patterns are matched against spaCy's tokens, and an attribute can only match when a component of the pipeline sets it: DEP needs the parser, for instance, and spaCy gives an error when the component is missing. Patterns that ask for an entity type (ENT_TYPE or ENT_IOB) give a warning when no component sets entities, as after spacy_initialize(entity = FALSE), since they then match nothing. The labels of tags and dependency relations differ between language models; spacy_parse(x, tag = TRUE, dependency = TRUE) shows those of the model in use. A match is only as good as the model's annotation of the text.

The values of spaCy's set operators (IN, NOT_IN, IS_SUBSET, IS_SUPERSET and INTERSECTS) can be vectors of any length, and whole numbers need not be integers, as for as_entity_patterns().

Phrases are split into tokens by spaCy's tokenizer, and match the same sequence of tokens in a document, as described for as_entity_patterns(). They are matched with spaCy's PhraseMatcher, which stays fast for many thousands of phrases. A phrase that matches in any case, as dictionary values do, is tokenized as it is written, and spaCy's tokenizer can split the same word differently in another case: it keeps "Inc." as one token but splits "inc." into two, so the phrase "acme widgets, inc." does not match the text "Acme Widgets, Inc.", while the phrase "Acme Widgets, Inc." in any case does. A warning is given when a component of the pipeline, such as merge_entities, changes the tokens of the documents, since phrases may then not match.

Matching adds little to the time that parsing takes, except for many token patterns: a few thousand make it much slower, so give phrases as phrases where you can, not as token patterns. Dictionary values with wildcards are token patterns, but those of a single word are combined into one for each label. Patterns that need no entities are faster after spacy_initialize(entity = FALSE).

See also

spacy_extract_dependency_matches() for tokens connected in the dependency parse; as_entity_patterns() and spacy_initialize() to make matches named entities.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
spacy_initialize()

txt <- c(doc1 = "The book was written by Jane. Jane wrote the book.",
         doc2 = "Mistakes were made, and the report is being rewritten.")

# passive verbs, by the dependency and tag labels of the English models:
# a passive auxiliary, any adverbs or further auxiliaries, and a past
# participle
passive <- list(
  PASSIVE = list(list(DEP = "auxpass"),
                 list(DEP = list(IN = c("advmod", "neg", "aux", "auxpass")),
                      OP = "*"),
                 list(TAG = "VBN"))
)
spacy_extract_matches(txt, passive)

# two labels, the second with alternative patterns
spacy_extract_matches(txt, list(
  DET_NOUN = list(list(POS = "DET"), list(POS = "NOUN")),
  WRITE = list(list(list(LEMMA = "write")),
               list(list(LEMMA = "rewrite")))
))

# phrases, matched exactly or in any case
spacy_extract_matches(txt, as_entity_patterns(c(TITLE = "the book")))
spacy_extract_matches(txt, as_entity_patterns(c(TITLE = "the book"),
                                              case_insensitive = TRUE))

# a quanteda dictionary, with its wildcards
dict <- quanteda::dictionary(list(writing = c("writ*", "wrote", "the book"),
                                  error = "mistake*"))
spacy_extract_matches(txt, dict)
} # }
